reconcile.connective: JFB holds this was Jesus' one and only Nazareth visit, the very scene Luke narrates, against the majority-harmonist two-visit view.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman argues Luke deliberately relocated Mark's midpoint Nazareth episode to the ministry's opening for theological effect, not literal chronology.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them)
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them) (HarperOne, 2009)

excerpts.excerpt_text: This, according to the majority of Harmonists, was the second of two visits which our Lord paid to Nazareth during His public ministry; but in our view it was His first and only visit to it.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the harmonist debate over whether Matthew/Mark's Nazareth episode is a distinct second visit or the very event Luke narrates first — the crux of the chronological-placement tension.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Matthew 13:54
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB engages the placement question head-on at this very verse, weighing the majority two-visit harmonist view against their own one-visit reading.
